simple.meaning: כְּלוּב (kᵉlûwb) is a Hebrew animal word meaning “a bird-trap (as furnished with a clap-stick or treadle to spring it); hence, a basket (as resembling a wicker cage).” BibleIQ follows the concrete thing through the verses where it appears.
simple.biblicalBackground: The occurrence trail begins at Jeremiah 5:27. The background is built from the passages where the word occurs.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to כְּלוּב (H3619) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Concrete words often carry patterns through Scripture because objects, animals, offerings, and created things are used repeatedly in worship, judgment, covenant, and narrative.

timeline.evidenceText: As a cage is full of birds, so are their houses full of deceit. Therefore they have become great, and grew rich.
Thus the Lord Yahweh showed me: behold, a basket of summer fruit.
